column3: The word for "I" and "me": Chinese does not change the pronoun between subject and object, so 我 is the same in 我看他 and 他看我. 我 began as a picture of a trident-like weapon (perhaps a three-bladed polearm, two scholars suggest) and was borrowed for its sound to write "I" as early as the oracle bones.
column9: The word for "I" and "me": Chinese does not change the pronoun between subject and object, so 我 is the same in 我看他 and 他看我. 我 began as a picture of a trident-like weapon (perhaps a three-bladed polearm, two scholars suggest) and was borrowed for its sound to write "I" as early as the oracle bones.

column3: You. The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 尔 probably gives the sound; the same 亻 starts 他, 们 and 住. For more than one person add 们: 你们. For someone you want to treat with respect there is 您.
column9: You. The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 尔 probably gives the sound; the same 亻 starts 他, 們 and 住. For more than one person add 們: 你們. For someone you want to treat with respect there is 您.

column3: He or "him". The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 也 gives the sound. 他 and 她 are both said tā, so in speech only the context tells you which is meant; only the writing differs.
column9: He or "him". The 亻 (person) gives the meaning and 也 gives the sound. 他 and 她 are both said tā, so in speech only the context tells you which is meant; only the writing differs.

column3: She or "her". It is 女 (woman) next to the same 也 that is in 他, so the two characters differ only on the left. Said tā, exactly like 他.
column9: She or "her". It is 女 (woman) next to the same 也 that is in 他, so the two characters differ only on the left. Said tā, exactly like 他.

column3: A polite "you" for one person, used to show respect: 您好, 请问您贵姓. It is 你 written above 心 (heart), which fits its respectful tone. Use it for a single person only; for a group say 你们.
column9: A polite "you" for one person, used to show respect: 您好, 請問您貴姓. It is 你 written above 心 (heart), which fits its respectful tone. Use it for a single person only; for a group say 你們.

column3: Added after 我, 你, 他 or a word for people to make a plural: 我们, 孩子们. Do not use it together with a number: 三个孩子, not 三个孩子们. 亻 (people) gives the meaning and 门 (mén) gives the sound. It is read men, with no tone.
column9: Added after 我, 你, 他 or a word for people to make a plural: 我們, 孩子們. Do not use it together with a number: 三個孩子, not 三個孩子們. 亻 (people) gives the meaning and 門 (mén) gives the sound. It is read men, with no tone.

column3: We or "us": 我 plus the plural ending 们, which is light, so it is read wǒmen. Put 的 after it to say "our": 我们的老师.
column9: We or "us": 我 plus the plural ending 們, which is light, so it is read wǒmen. Put 的 after it to say "our": 我們的老師.

column3: You for two or more people: 你 plus 们. It works as subject, object and, with 的, as "your": 你们的老师. For one person use 你, or 您 to be polite.
column9: You for two or more people: 你 plus 們. It works as subject, object and, with 的, as "your": 你們的老師. For one person use 你, or 您 to be polite.

column3: They for a group of men, or a group of men and women together. If everyone in the group is female, 她们 is used instead. Both are said tāmen.
column9: They for a group of men, or a group of men and women together. If everyone in the group is female, 她們 is used instead. Both are said tāmen.

column3: They for a group made up only of women or girls; for a mixed group the writing uses 他们. Said exactly like 他们, so it is a distinction of the written language.
column9: They for a group made up only of women or girls; for a mixed group the writing uses 他們. Said exactly like 他們, so it is a distinction of the written language.

column3: Good or "well", and on its own the answer "OK, fine". It is 女 (woman) and 子 (child); the usual explanation is that a woman with a child was seen as good. Read hǎo here; as "to like" it is read hào, as in 爱好.
column7: The weather is very nice today.
column9: Good or "well", and on its own the answer "OK, fine". It is 女 (woman) and 子 (child); the usual explanation is that a woman with a child was seen as good. Read hǎo here; as "to like" it is read hào, as in 愛好.

column3: Thank you. The word 谢 is said twice and the second is light: xièxie. The usual reply is 不客气. In 谢, 讠 (speech) gives the meaning and 射 the sound.
column9: Thank you. The word 謝 is said twice and the second is light: xièxie. The usual reply is 不客氣. In 謝, 言 (speech) gives the meaning and 射 the sound.

column3: The usual reply to 谢谢: "you're welcome". It is 不 plus 客气 ("to stand on ceremony, be polite"), so it means "no need to be formal". In 客 (guest), 宀 (roof) sits over 各, which gives the sound.
column9: The usual reply to 謝謝: "you're welcome". It is 不 plus 客氣 ("to stand on ceremony, be polite"), so it means "no need to be formal". In 客 (guest), 宀 (roof) sits over 各, which gives the sound.

column3: Sorry, for a mistake or for bumping into someone: it says you have let the other person down, the opposite of 对得起. The usual answer is 没关系; 不好意思 is a lighter "sorry". It is not used for sympathy, as in "I'm sorry to hear that".
column9: Sorry, for a mistake or for bumping into someone: it says you have let the other person down, the opposite of 對得起. The usual answer is 沒關係; 不好意思 is a lighter "sorry". It is not used for sympathy, as in "I'm sorry to hear that".

column3: It doesn't matter: the answer to 对不起. Literally "no connection": 没 (not have) plus 关系 (relationship). Close in use to 没事 and 不要紧, which also say "no problem".
column9: It doesn't matter: the answer to 對不起. Literally "no connection": 沒 (not have) plus 關係 (relationship). Close in use to 沒事 and 不要緊, which also say "no problem".

column3: It's nothing, said after thanks or an apology to wave it away. Literally "not have anything": 没 plus 什么 (what, here "anything"). It can also mean "nothing in particular".
column9: It's nothing, said after thanks or an apology to wave it away. Literally "not have anything": 沒 plus 什麼 (what, here "anything"). It can also mean "nothing in particular".

column3: Goodbye, literally "again see". The 见 alone means "see". Casually, people also say 拜拜, or 明天见 "see you tomorrow".
column9: Goodbye, literally "again see". The 見 alone means "see". Casually, people also say 拜拜, or 明天見 "see you tomorrow". 見 shows a kneeling person with a big eye for a head.

column3: Please: put it before a verb to ask politely, as in 请坐. It also means "to invite" or "to treat": 我请你吃饭 is "my treat". 讠 (speech) gives the meaning and 青 the sound (qīng, close to qǐng).
column9: Please: put it before a verb to ask politely, as in 請坐. It also means "to invite" or "to treat": 我請你吃飯 is "my treat". 言 (speech) gives the meaning and 青 the sound (qīng, close to qǐng).

column3: Excuse me, may I ask: said before a question to someone you do not know. Literally "please ask". In 问, 口 (mouth) gives the meaning and 门 (mén) gives the sound, close to wèn.
column7: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
column9: Excuse me, may I ask: said before a question to someone you do not know. Literally "please ask". In 問, 口 (mouth) gives the meaning and 門 (mén) gives the sound, close to wèn.

column3: Please come in, said to someone at the door. The 辶 in 进 (walk) is the meaning part. To a guest who has come in, the next words are often 请坐 "please sit".
column7: Please come in and sit down.
column9: Please come in, said to someone at the door. The 辶 in 進 (walk) is the meaning part. To a guest who has come in, the next words are often 請坐 "please sit".

column3: Please sit down, what a host says to a guest. 坐 has 土 (earth, ground) at the bottom. After 坐 you can add the place: 请坐这里.
column9: Please sit down, what a host says to a guest. 坐 has 土 (earth, ground) at the bottom. After 坐 you can add the place: 請坐這裡.

column3: One: an ideogram, a single horizontal stroke. 二 and 三 add strokes. The tone changes in speech (yí before a fourth tone, yì before the others: 一个 yí gè, 一天 yì tiān) but dictionaries write yī.
column9: One: an ideogram, a single horizontal stroke. 二 and 三 add strokes. The tone changes in speech (yí before a fourth tone, yì before the others: 一個 yí gè, 一天 yì tiān) but dictionaries write yī.

column3: Two: two parallel strokes. Use 二 for counting and in numbers (二十, 第二, 二月), but 两 before a measure word: 两个人, not 二个人.
column6: Jīntiān shì èr yuè èr hào.
column9: Two: two parallel strokes. Use 二 for counting and in numbers (二十, 第二, 二月), but 兩 before a measure word: 兩個人, not 二個人.

column3: Three: three parallel strokes. A number goes in front of a measure word: 三个人, 三本书. 三 is also the base of 星期三 (Wednesday).
column9: Three: three parallel strokes. A number goes in front of a measure word: 三個人, 三本書. 三 is also the base of 星期三 (Wednesday).

column3: Four. 四 began as a picture of a nose breathing out and was borrowed for the number because of its sound; older writing used four stacked strokes, which was too easy to mix up with 二 and 三.
column9: Four. 四 began as a picture of a nose breathing out and was borrowed for the number because of its sound; older writing used four stacked strokes, which was too easy to mix up with 二 and 三.

column3: Five. There are several theories (a tally mark, the palm lines of a hand) and none is settled, so treat it as a shape to memorize. 五 is also the base of 星期五 (Friday).
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
column7: There are five people in my family.
column9: Five. There are several theories (a tally mark, the palm lines of a hand) and none is settled, so treat it as a shape to memorize. 五 is also the base of 星期五 (Friday).

column3: Six. Two ideas are offered, a picture of a shed or an old counting symbol, and neither is certain. 星期六 is Saturday.
column9: Six. Two ideas are offered, a picture of a shed or an old counting symbol, and neither is certain. 星期六 is Saturday.

column3: Seven. It is a horizontal and a vertical stroke crossing, originally the character for 切 "to cut". Unlike 十, the vertical stroke of 七 ends in a bend (乚).
column9: Seven. It is a horizontal and a vertical stroke crossing, originally the character for 切 "to cut". Unlike 十, the vertical stroke of 七 ends in a bend (乚).

column3: Eight. It is two bent lines meaning "to divide", later borrowed for the number because of the sound. The idea of dividing is still visible in 半 and 分, which both contain 八.
column9: Eight. It is two bent lines meaning "to divide", later borrowed for the number because of the sound. The idea of dividing is still visible in 半 and 分, which both contain 八.

column3: Nine. It is a picture of an arm bent at the elbow (the hook at the lower right is the bend); the word for "elbow" is now written 肘.
column9: Nine. It is a picture of an arm bent at the elbow (the hook at the lower right is the bend); the word for "elbow" is now written 肘.

column3: Ten: a crossing of a horizontal and a vertical stroke; early forms were a single vertical stroke and the origin is debated. 11-19 are 十 plus a digit (十一), 20-90 a digit plus 十 (二十).
column9: Ten: a crossing of a horizontal and a vertical stroke; early forms were a single vertical stroke and the origin is debated. 11-19 are 十 plus a digit (十一), 20-90 a digit plus 十 (二十).

column3: Zero, and the word for a gap in the middle of a number: 105 is 一百零五. 雨 (rain) gives the meaning and 令 the sound, which is líng in both.
column6: Zhè běn shū yībǎi líng wǔ kuài.
column9: Zero, and the word for a gap in the middle of a number: 105 is 一百零五. 雨 (rain) gives the meaning and 令 the sound, which is líng in both.

column3: A circle used as a written zero. It is how years and phone numbers are read digit by digit: 二〇〇〇年 is èr líng líng líng nián. 零 is the same sound and is used in counting, as in 一百零五.
column6: Wǒ èr líng líng líng nián chūshēng.
column9: A circle used as a written zero. It is how years and phone numbers are read digit by digit: 二〇〇〇年 is èr líng líng líng nián. 零 is the same sound and is used in counting, as in 一百零五.

column3: Two before a measure word: 两个人, 两本书; use 二 for counting and in numbers. It also means "a couple of": 过两天 is "in a couple of days".
column9: Two before a measure word: 兩個人, 兩本書; use 二 for counting and in numbers. It also means "a couple of": 過兩天 is "in a couple of days".

column3: Hundred: 一 on top of 白. 白 is the sound part (bǎi against bái). You must keep the 一 for 100: say 一百, not just 百.
column7: This cup is a hundred yuan.
column9: Hundred: 一 on top of 白. 白 is the sound part (bǎi against bái). You must keep the 一 for 100: say 一百, not just 百.

column3: How many, asked about a small number (about ten or fewer): 几个人? For larger or open quantities use 多少. A measure word follows it: 几本书; it also asks 几岁 (a child's age) and 几月 "which month".
column7: How many friends do you have?
column9: How many, asked about a small number (about ten or fewer): 幾個人? For larger or open quantities use 多少. A measure word follows it: 幾本書; it also asks 幾歲 (a child's age) and 幾月 "which month".

column3: How many or "how much", for any size of quantity. Literally "many-few". The second syllable is light: duōshao. The standard question for prices is 多少钱？
column9: How many or "how much", for any size of quantity. Literally "many-few". The second syllable is light: duōshao. The standard question for prices is 多少錢？

column3: Half. 八 (divide) over 牛 (ox): it is read as cutting an ox in two. In 半个小时 the 半 comes before the measure word, but "an hour and a half" is 一个半小时. 三点半 is half past three.
column9: Half. 八 (divide) over 牛 (ox): it is read as cutting an ox in two. In 半個小時 the 半 comes before the measure word, but "an hour and a half" is 一個半小時. 三點半 is half past three.

column3: Put before a number to make an ordinal: 第一, 第二个. ⺮ (bamboo) on top is the meaning part, standing for the bamboo strips used to write on, and 弟 gives the sound; both are read dì.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ dìyī cì lái.
column7: This is my first time here.
column9: Put before a number to make an ordinal: 第一, 第二個. ⺮ (bamboo) on top is the meaning part, standing for the bamboo strips used to write on, and 弟 gives the sound; both are read dì.

column3: Person. It is a side view of a standing person. At the left of other characters it shrinks to 亻 (你, 他, 住, 休). Add it to a country to name its people: 中国人.
column7: There are a lot of people here.
column9: Person. It is a side view of a standing person. At the left of other characters it shrinks to 亻 (你, 他, 住, 休). Add it to a country to name its people: 中國人.

column3: Male. 田 (field) over 力 (strength): it is read as the person who supplies the strength to work a field. It pairs with 女, and starts 男人, 男生 and 男朋友.
column9: Male. 田 (field) over 力 (strength): it is read as the person who supplies the strength to work a field. It pairs with 女, and starts 男人, 男生 and 男朋友.

column3: Female. It is a picture of a woman with folded arms, kneeling or standing. As the left part of other characters it marks women and female relatives: 妈, 姐, 妹, 奶, 好. Pinyin is nǚ (typed nv).
column6: Tā shì yī wèi nǚ yīshēng.
column9: Female. It is a picture of a woman with folded arms, kneeling or standing. As the left part of other characters it marks women and female relatives: 媽, 姐, 妹, 奶, 好. Pinyin is nǚ (typed nv).

column3: Mom, as a form of address (妈！) or with a possessive (我妈). 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 马 (mǎ) gives the sound, close to mā.
column9: Mom, as a form of address (媽！) or with a possessive (我媽). 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 馬 (mǎ) gives the sound, close to mā.

column3: Mom. Family terms are often doubled (爸爸, 哥哥, 姐姐, 弟弟, 妹妹), and the second syllable is light: māma. Chinese says 爸爸妈妈, with father first.
column9: Mom. Family terms are often doubled (爸爸, 哥哥, 姐姐, 弟弟, 妹妹), and the second syllable is light: māma. Chinese says 爸爸媽媽, with father first.

column3: Dad, as a form of address (爸！) or with a possessive (我爸). 父 (father) on top gives the meaning and 巴 (bā) gives the sound, close to bà. The same 巴 is in 吧.
column9: Dad, as a form of address (爸！) or with a possessive (我爸). 父 (father) on top gives the meaning and 巴 (bā) gives the sound, close to bà. The same 巴 is in 吧.

column3: Dad, with a light second syllable: bàba. 爸 is a colloquial form of 父 (father), which is why it is built from 父 plus a sound part.
column9: Dad, with a light second syllable: bàba. 爸 is a colloquial form of 父 (father), which is why it is built from 父 plus a sound part.

column3: Older brother. It is two 可 stacked; the character first meant "to sing, song" and the sense "older brother" is a later borrowing. The "song" meaning survives in 歌, which has 哥 as its sound part.
column6: Wǒ gē bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
column7: My older brother is three years older than me.
column9: Older brother. It is two 可 stacked; the character first meant "to sing, song" and the sense "older brother" is a later borrowing. The "song" meaning survives in 歌, which has 哥 as its sound part.

column3: Older brother, with a light second syllable: gēge. Chinese always says whether a sibling is older or younger: 哥哥 and 姐姐 are older, 弟弟 and 妹妹 are younger.
column7: My older brother works in Beijing.
column9: Older brother, with a light second syllable: gēge. Chinese always says whether a sibling is older or younger: 哥哥 and 姐姐 are older, 弟弟 and 妹妹 are younger.

column3: Older sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 且 the sound, though qiě and jiě are only loosely alike. Alone it turns up in 小姐 and as an address after a name; the everyday word is 姐姐.
column7: My older sister is a teacher.
column9: Older sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 且 the sound, though qiě and jiě are only loosely alike. Alone it turns up in 小姐 and as an address after a name; the everyday word is 姐姐.

column3: Older sister, with a light second syllable: jiějie. It is also what you may call a young woman a little older than you who is not a relative.
column7: My older sister is taller than me.
column9: Older sister, with a light second syllable: jiějie. It is also what you may call a young woman a little older than you who is not a relative.

column3: Younger brother. It is a picture of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping suggested order or sequence, which stretched to "the one after", a younger brother. 第 (the ordinal marker) is 弟 with ⺮ on top and sounds the same, dì.
column7: My younger brother is at school.
column9: Younger brother. It is a picture of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping suggested order or sequence, which stretched to "the one after", a younger brother. 第 (the ordinal marker) is 弟 with ⺮ on top and sounds the same, dì.

column3: Younger brother, with a light second syllable: dìdi. It is also what you may call a boy a bit younger than you. In the pair 哥哥 / 弟弟 Chinese always says older or younger.
column6: Dìdi bǐ wǒ xiǎo liǎng suì.
column7: My younger brother is two years younger than me.
column9: Younger brother, with a light second syllable: dìdi. It is also what you may call a boy a bit younger than you. In the pair 哥哥 / 弟弟 Chinese always says older or younger.

column3: Younger sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 未 gives the sound (wèi against mèi). Alone it appears in forms like 我妹 and 妹妹, which is the everyday word.
column7: My younger sister is ten this year.
column9: Younger sister. 女 (woman) gives the meaning and 未 gives the sound (wèi against mèi). Alone it appears in forms like 我妹 and 妹妹, which is the everyday word.

column3: Younger sister, with a light second syllable: mèimei. The 女 on the left marks the female relative and 未 is the sound part, as in 妹.
column9: Younger sister, with a light second syllable: mèimei. The 女 on the left marks the female relative and 未 is the sound part, as in 妹.

column3: Grandmother on the father's side (the father's mother). 奶 has 女 (woman) as meaning part and 乃 as sound part (both nǎi); by itself 奶 means "milk", as in 牛奶.
column7: My grandmother is seventy this year.
column9: Grandmother on the father's side (the father's mother). 奶 has 女 (woman) as meaning part and 乃 as sound part (both nǎi); by itself 奶 means "milk", as in 牛奶.

column3: Grandfather on the father's side. The 父 (father) on top is the meaning part. The second 爷 is light: yéye. The mother's father is 外公, and the father's mother is 奶奶.
column7: Grandpa is watching TV at home.
column9: Grandfather on the father's side. The 父 (father) on top is the meaning part. The second 爺 is light: yéye. The mother's father is 外公, and the father's mother is 奶奶.

column3: Son. 儿 and 子 both mean "child", so it is "child-child". 子 is light: érzi. Here 儿 is a full syllable, not the ending of words like 这儿.
column9: Son. 兒 and 子 both mean "child", so it is "child-child". 子 is light: érzi. Here 兒 is a full syllable, not the ending of words like 這兒.

column3: Daughter: 女 (female) plus 儿 (child). In pinyin an apostrophe splits the syllables so they do not run together: nǚ'ér.
column9: Daughter: 女 (female) plus 兒 (child). In pinyin an apostrophe splits the syllables so they do not run together: nǚ'ér.

column3: Child, kid, also "one's children": 你有孩子吗？ 孩 has 子 (child) as meaning part and 亥 as sound part (hài, close to hái). The final 子 is light.
column9: Child, kid, also "one's children": 你有孩子嗎？ 孩 has 子 (child) as meaning part and 亥 as sound part (hài, close to hái). The final 子 is light.

column3: A light ending that makes many nouns: 桌子, 房子, 杯子, 孩子. It has no meaning of its own there. Read zǐ it means "child; son". The shape is a baby with a big head, spread arms and legs wrapped in a blanket.
column9: A light ending that makes many nouns: 桌子, 房子, 杯子, 孩子. It has no meaning of its own there. Read zǐ it means "child; son". The shape is a baby with a big head, spread arms and legs wrapped in a blanket.

column3: Family members: 家 (home) plus 人 (people). 一家人 is "a family, all of one household". In 家, 宀 (roof) sits over what is now written 豕 (pig), though that bottom part was originally a sound part.
column9: Family members: 家 (home) plus 人 (people). 一家人 is "a family, all of one household". In 家, 宀 (roof) sits over what is now written 豕 (pig), though that bottom part was originally a sound part.

column3: This. Before a noun it normally needs a measure word: 这个人, 这本书. In speech it is often said zhèi, especially before a measure word. 辶 (walk) is the part on the left.
column9: This. Before a noun it normally needs a measure word: 這個人, 這本書. In speech it is often said zhèi, especially before a measure word. 辶 (walk) is the part on the left.

column3: That. The 阝 on the right is the "city" part, because the character was first the name of a state; it was later borrowed for "that". 这 is near, 那 is far. Read nà; the question word 哪 (nǎ) is 那 with 口 added.
column9: That. The 阝 on the right is the "city" part, because the character was first the name of a state; it was later borrowed for "that". 這 is near, 那 is far. Read nà; the question word 哪 (nǎ) is 那 with 口 added.

column3: Here, said zhèr: the spoken ending 儿 fuses with zhè and has no tone of its own. It means the same as 这里.
column9: Here, said zhèr: the spoken ending 兒 fuses with zhè and has no tone of its own. It means the same as 這裡.

column3: There, said nàr. The opposite of 这儿. Use it with 在 for locations: 我的书在那儿. Do not confuse with 哪儿 (nǎr, "where"), which has 口 added and a different tone.
column9: There, said nàr. The opposite of 這兒. Use it with 在 for locations: 我的書在那兒. Do not confuse with 哪兒 (nǎr, "where"), which has 口 added and a different tone.

column3: Here. It means the same as 这儿. Heard as zhèli. Its partners are 那里 "there" and 哪里 "where".
column9: Here. It means the same as 這兒. Heard as zhèli. Its partners are 那裡 "there" and 哪裡 "where".

column3: There, the same meaning as 那儿. The 里 is light in speech and does not mean "inside" here; it just makes a place word.
column7: There is a shop over there.
column9: There, the same meaning as 那兒. The 裡 is light in speech and does not mean "inside" here; it just makes a place word.

column3: These. 些 means "some, several" and is already a plural measure, so the noun follows directly: 这些书, with no 个. Used alone it also works as a pronoun: 这些是我的.
column6: Zhèxiē shū dōu shì xīn de.
column9: These. 些 means "some, several" and is already a plural measure, so the noun follows directly: 這些書, with no 個. Used alone it also works as a pronoun: 這些是我的.

column3: Those: 那 plus 些, a plural measure, so no 个 before the noun: 那些人. It can also stand alone as a pronoun: 那些是我的衣服.
column9: Those: 那 plus 些, a plural measure, so no 個 before the noun: 那些人. It can also stand alone as a pronoun: 那些是我的衣服.

column3: This side, over here: 这边请 is "this way, please". 边 means "side": 辶 (walk) is its meaning part. The partners are 那边 "over there" and 哪边 "which side?".
column9: This side, over here: 這邊請 is "this way, please". 邊 means "side": 辶 (walk) is its meaning part. The partners are 那邊 "over there" and 哪邊 "which side?".

column3: That side, over there. The 边 is light: nàbian. Often used to point things out against 这边: 这边是学校，那边是商店.
column7: There is a station over there.
column9: That side, over there. The 邊 is light: nàbian. Often used to point things out against 這邊: 這邊是學校，那邊是商店.

column3: What. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你吃什么？ ("you eat what?"). Before a noun it asks "what kind": 什么书？
column7: What do you want to eat?
column9: What. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你吃什麼？ ("you eat what?"). Before a noun it asks "what kind": 什麼書？

column3: Who. It is read shéi in speech; shuí is another reading. 讠 (speech) is the meaning part, and 隹 on the right is the sound part.
column9: Who. It is read shéi in speech; shuí is another reading. 言 (speech) is the meaning part, and 隹 on the right is the sound part.

column3: Which: put it before a measure word, 哪个, 哪本书. It is 那 (nà) with 口 (mouth) added, so the two look alike and differ in sound only by tone, nǎ against nà. Only the 口 tells a question from a pointing word.
column9: Which: put it before a measure word, 哪個, 哪本書. It is 那 (nà) with 口 (mouth) added, so the two look alike and differ in sound only by tone, nǎ against nà. Only the 口 tells a question from a pointing word.

column3: Where, said nǎr. Ask for a place with 你去哪儿？ or 你在哪儿？ Compare 那儿 (nàr, "there"), which is the same without the 口.
column9: Where, said nǎr. Ask for a place with 你去哪兒？ or 你在哪兒？ Compare 那兒 (nàr, "there"), which is the same without the 口.

column3: Where, the same meaning as 哪儿. Said twice, 哪里哪里, it is a modest reply to a compliment, "not at all".
column9: Where, the same meaning as 哪兒. Said twice, 哪裡哪裡, it is a modest reply to a compliment, "not at all".

column3: Which ones (plural), for choosing among several things: 哪些书？ The noun follows directly, without 个. For a single thing say 哪个.
column9: Which ones (plural), for choosing among several things: 哪些書？ The noun follows directly, without 個. For a single thing say 哪個.

column3: How or "why": 去机场怎么走？ asks how to go; 你怎么了？ asks what is wrong. 心 (heart) is the meaning part of 怎, and 乍 the sound. Before the verb it asks about way, not reason.
column7: How do I get to the airport?
column9: How or "why": 去機場怎麼走？ asks how to go; 你怎麼了？ asks what is wrong. 心 (heart) is the meaning part of 怎, and 乍 the sound. Before the verb it asks about way, not reason.

column3: What are you doing? or "what for?", a spoken phrase: 你在干什么？ This 干 is gàn ("do"); the other 干 is gān ("dry").
column9: What are you doing? or "what for?", a spoken phrase: 你在幹什麼？ This 幹 is gàn ("do"); the other 乾 is gān ("dry").

column3: A question that expects "yes": 你是不是累了？ It is 是 + 不 + 是, the "verb, not, verb" way of asking. The middle 不 is light: shìbushì. Add it to the end of a statement to check it: 他是老师，是不是？
column9: A question that expects "yes": 你是不是累了？ It is 是 + 不 + 是, the "verb, not, verb" way of asking. The middle 不 is light: shìbushì. Add it to the end of a statement to check it: 他是老師，是不是？

column3: To be. It links two nouns: 我是学生. It is not used before an adjective: say 我很高兴, not 我是高兴. The origin is unclear, so there is nothing to read from the shape.
column9: To be. It links two nouns: 我是學生. It is not used before an adjective: say 我很高興, not 我是高興. The origin is unclear, so there is nothing to read from the shape.

column3: To have and "there is": 我有一本书; 桌子上有一本书. Its negative is 没有, never 不有. Its hand, once written 又 (yòu), gives the sound, and its 月 is a changed 肉 "meat".
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
column7: There are four people in my family.
column9: To have and "there is": 我有一本書; 桌子上有一本書. Its negative is 沒有, never 不有. Its hand, once written 又 (yòu), gives the sound, and its 月 is a changed 肉 "meat".

column3: At, in, be located: 我在家. Before a verb it gives the place of the action (我在学校学习) or marks an action in progress (他在吃饭).
column9: At, in, be located: 我在家. Before a verb it gives the place of the action (我在學校學習) or marks an action in progress (他在吃飯).

column3: Not, no. Put it before verbs and adjectives: 不好. Before another fourth tone it is said bú (不是 is bú shì), but dictionaries write bù. It is a picture of a flower's calyx, borrowed for the word "not".
column9: Not, no. Put it before verbs and adjectives: 不好. Before another fourth tone it is said bú (不是 is bú shì), but dictionaries write bù. It is a picture of a flower's calyx, borrowed for the word "not".

column3: Not (have): negates 有 and past actions: 我没吃, 我没有书. Never use 不 for past actions. 氵 (water) is the left part of 没.
column9: Not (have): negates 有 and past actions: 我沒吃, 我沒有書. Never use 不 for past actions. 氵 (water) is the left part of 沒.

column3: Does not have, "there is no", and the negative of past actions: 他没有来 ("he did not come"). At the end of a question it asks "did you or not": 你吃了没有？
column7: I don't have an older brother.
column9: Does not have, "there is no", and the negative of past actions: 他沒有來 ("he did not come"). At the end of a question it asks "did you or not": 你吃了沒有？

column3: Correct, right: 你说得对. Also "toward, to": 他对我很好 ("he is good to me"). The opposite is 错 "wrong"; 对不对? asks "right?".
column6: Zhè ge zì duì bu duì?
column9: Correct, right: 你說得對. Also "toward, to": 他對我很好 ("he is good to me"). The opposite is 錯 "wrong"; 對不對? asks "right?".

column3: Wrong, mistaken, the opposite of 对: 写错了. 钅 (metal) is the meaning part and 昔 the sound (xī). It follows a verb to say how it went: 说错, 写错.
column9: Wrong, mistaken, the opposite of 對: 寫錯了. 釒 (metal) is the meaning part and 昔 the sound (xī). It follows a verb to say how it went: 說錯, 寫錯.

column3: Not right, wrong: 这个字不对. Also said to stop someone: 不对！ ("wait, that's wrong"). Before a fourth tone 不 is said bú: bú duì.
column9: Not right, wrong: 這個字不對. Also said to stop someone: 不對！ ("wait, that's wrong"). Before a fourth tone 不 is said bú: bú duì.

column3: Not big: 房间不大. In speech it can also mean "not very": 不大好 "not very good". 大 is the opposite of 小.
column9: Not big: 房間不大. In speech it can also mean "not very": 不大好 "not very good". 大 is the opposite of 小.

column3: No need to: 不用谢 ("no need to thank me"), 不用去 ("you don't have to go"). It is 不 plus 用 ("use"); the answer to an offer of help can be 不用，谢谢.
column9: No need to: 不用謝 ("no need to thank me"), 不用去 ("you don't have to go"). It is 不 plus 用 ("use"); the answer to an offer of help can be 不用，謝謝.

column3: Also, too. It goes after the subject, before the verb: 我也是学生. With 都 the order is 也都: 他们也都是学生. There are several unrelated theories for the shape, so treat it as a shape to memorize.
column9: Also, too. It goes after the subject, before the verb: 我也是學生. With 都 the order is 也都: 他們也都是學生. There are several unrelated theories for the shape, so treat it as a shape to memorize.

column3: All, both: it comes after the group it covers and before the verb: 我们都是学生. 阝 on the right is the meaning part ("city") and 者 the sound. Read dū it means "capital city".
column9: All, both: it comes after the group it covers and before the verb: 我們都是學生. 阝 on the right is the meaning part ("city") and 者 the sound. Read dū it means "capital city".

column3: Very. With an adjective it is almost required in a plain statement: 她很高; just 她高 sounds like a comparison. Then 很 is often weak, close to "is". 彳 (step) is the meaning part and 艮 the sound.
column9: Very. With an adjective it is almost required in a plain statement: 她很高; just 她高 sounds like a comparison. Then 很 is often weak, close to "is". 彳 (step) is the meaning part and 艮 the sound.

column3: Too, excessively: 太贵了. Usually with 了 at the end; 太好了！ means "great!". 太 was made from 大 by adding a dot, so the two are easy to mix up when writing: 大 has no dot.
column9: Too, excessively: 太貴了. Usually with 了 at the end; 太好了！ means "great!". 太 was made from 大 by adding a dot, so the two are easy to mix up when writing: 大 has no dot.

column3: Extremely, used like 很 before adjectives: 非常好. Literally "not ordinary": 非 ("not") plus 常 ("ordinary"). 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways, later borrowed for "not".
column9: Extremely, used like 很 before adjectives: 非常好. Literally "not ordinary": 非 ("not") plus 常 ("ordinary"). 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways, later borrowed for "not".

column3: Really, truly: 真好吃. Put it before an adjective for emphasis. Older forms of 真 (a spoon and a tripod vessel) differ from the modern shape, so its present parts are no guide to the meaning.
column6: Zhè ge zì zhēn nán xiě.
column7: This character is really hard to write.
column9: Really, truly: 真好吃. Put it before an adjective for emphasis. Older forms of 真 (a spoon and a tripod vessel) differ from the modern shape, so its present parts are no guide to the meaning.

column3: Really, truly: as a question, 真的吗？ "really?"; as a statement, 我真的不知道. After a noun, 的 gives "real, genuine": 真的钱.
column9: Really, truly: as a question, 真的嗎？ "really?"; as a statement, 我真的不知道. After a noun, 的 gives "real, genuine": 真的錢.

column3: OK, will do, as an answer: 行，没问题. Also "allowed": 这样行吗？ Its opposite is 不行. It is a picture of a street crossing, split into 彳 and 亍. In 银行 (bank) it is read háng.
column7: Is it OK to go today?
column9: OK, will do, as an answer: 行，沒問題. Also "allowed": 這樣行嗎？ Its opposite is 不行. It is a picture of a street crossing, split into 彳 and 亍. In 銀行 (bank) it is read háng.

column3: Friend. Both characters are made of a pair: 朋 is two 月, which were once strings of cowrie shells, not moons, and 友 is two hands 又, read as friendship. The last syllable is light: péngyou.
column6: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
column9: Friend. Both characters are made of a pair: 朋 is two 月, which were once strings of cowrie shells, not moons, and 友 is two hands 又, read as friendship. The last syllable is light: péngyou.

column3: Boyfriend. It is a fixed word: 男 ("male") plus 朋友 does not simply mean a friend who is male. Say 我男朋友 or 我的男朋友.
column9: Boyfriend. It is a fixed word: 男 ("male") plus 朋友 does not simply mean a friend who is male. Say 我男朋友 or 我的男朋友.

column3: Girlfriend, the partner of 男朋友. It is a fixed word and does not just mean a friend who is a woman. Without 的 it is natural: 我女朋友.
column6: Tā de nǚ péngyou shì lǎoshī.
column9: Girlfriend, the partner of 男朋友. It is a fixed word and does not just mean a friend who is a woman. Without 的 it is natural: 我女朋友.

column3: Literally "little friend": a friendly word for a child, used by teachers and adults: 小朋友，你几岁了？ Plural 小朋友们 for a group. The last syllable is third tone here: xiǎopéngyǒu.
column7: Little one, how old are you?
column9: Literally "little friend": a friendly word for a child, used by teachers and adults: 小朋友，你幾歲了？ Plural 小朋友們 for a group. The last syllable is third tone here: xiǎopéngyǒu.

column3: Boy or "male student", the pair of 女生. 生 means "student" here, as in 学生. 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground, and means "to be born, to live".
column6: Wǒmen bān yǒu shí ge nánshēng.
column9: Boy or "male student", the pair of 女生. 生 means "student" here, as in 學生. 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground, and means "to be born, to live".

column3: Girl or "female student". Use it for girls at school and for young women; for an adult woman in general the word is 女人.
column6: Nàge nǚshēng shì wǒ de tóngxué.
column9: Girl or "female student". Use it for girls at school and for young women; for an adult woman in general the word is 女人.

column3: Man, an adult male. Not the same as 男生, which is a boy or a male student. The pair is 女人.
column9: Man, an adult male. Not the same as 男生, which is a boy or a male student. The pair is 女人.

column3: Woman, an adult female, the pair of 男人. It is a plain description. To address someone, use 小姐 or 老师 or the name instead.
column9: Woman, an adult female, the pair of 男人. It is a plain description. To address someone, use 小姐 or 老師 or the name instead.

column3: Boy. The 儿 turns the end of 孩 into an -r sound: nánháir. The same word without 儿, 男孩, is also used. 男 is 田 (field) over 力 (strength).
column9: Boy. The 兒 turns the end of 孩 into an -r sound: nánháir. The same word without 兒, 男孩, is also used. 男 is 田 (field) over 力 (strength).

column3: Girl, pronounced nǚháir. 孩 is 子 (child) with 亥 for sound. Add 小 for "little girl": 小女孩儿.
column6: Tā shì yī ge xiǎo nǚháir.
column9: Girl, pronounced nǚháir. 孩 is 子 (child) with 亥 for sound. Add 小 for "little girl": 小女孩兒.

column3: Child, little kid, said xiǎoháir. Told to an adult it means "you are not a child": 你不是小孩儿了.
column7: You are not a little kid anymore.
column9: Child, little kid, said xiǎoháir. Told to an adult it means "you are not a child": 你不是小孩兒了.

column3: Elderly person: 老 (old) plus 人. 老 shows, on one reading, an old man with long hair leaning on a cane (耂 on top, 匕 below). Use it for people: 照顾老人 "look after the elderly".
column6: Zhè wèi lǎorén shì wǒ de yéye.
column7: This elderly man is my grandpa.
column9: Elderly person: 老 (old) plus 人. 老 shows, on one reading, an old man with long hair leaning on a cane (耂 on top, 匕 below). Use it for people: 照顧老人 "look after the elderly".

column3: Miss or "young lady", a title put after a surname: 王小姐 is Miss Wang. It is a fixed word, not "little older sister", and the second syllable is light: xiǎojie.
column6: Wáng xiǎojie shì wǒmen de lǎoshī.
column9: Miss or "young lady", a title put after a surname: 王小姐 is Miss Wang. It is a fixed word, not "little older sister", and the second syllable is light: xiǎojie.

column3: Mr. or "sir": 王先生 is Mr. Wang. Literally "born earlier" (先 plus 生). 先 is a foot 止 stepping in front of a person 儿 (to go forward). The 生 is light: xiānsheng.
column9: Mr. or "sir": 王先生 is Mr. Wang. Literally "born earlier" (先 plus 生). 先 is a foot 止 stepping in front of a person 儿 (to go forward). The 生 is light: xiānsheng.

column3: Teacher, and also the way you address one, with or without a surname: 老师好！ 王老师. 老 ("old") shows respect here, and 师 means "master".
column9: Teacher, and also the way you address one, with or without a surname: 老師好！ 王老師. 老 ("old") shows respect here, and 師 means "master".

column3: Classmate, fellow student. Teachers also use it to address students: 同学们好！ 同 means "same" and 学 means "study". The bottom of 学 is 子 (child).
column9: Classmate, fellow student. Teachers also use it to address students: 同學們好！ 同 means "same" and 學 means "study". The bottom of 學 is 子 (child).

column3: Doctor (the person): 王医生. To see a doctor is 看医生. The hospital is 医院 and a nurse is 护士.
column7: I'm going to see the doctor tomorrow.
column9: Doctor (the person): 王醫生. To see a doctor is 看醫生. The hospital is 醫院 and a nurse is 護士.

column3: Worker, a person doing manual or factory work: 工 plus 人. 工 is a picture of a tool (a spade or a carpenter's square).
column9: Worker, a person doing manual or factory work: 工 plus 人. 工 is a picture of a tool (a spade or a carpenter's square).

column3: Patient, sick person: 病 (illness) plus 人. In 病, 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).
column6: Yīyuàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō bìngrén.
column7: There are a lot of patients in the hospital.
column9: Patient, sick person: 病 (illness) plus 人. In 病, 疒 (sickness) is the meaning part and 丙 the sound (bǐng, close to bìng).

column3: Someone you know through the internet, even if you have since met in person: 我昨天和网友见面了. Also anyone posting online, "netizens": 网友们的看法不同. 网 (net) plus 友 (friend).
column9: Someone you know through the internet, even if you have since met in person: 我昨天和網友見面了. Also anyone posting online, "netizens": 網友們的看法不同. 網 (net) plus 友 (friend).

column3: Other people, someone else: 别人的书 "other people's books". Here 别 means "other"; before a verb it means "don't". On the right is 刂 (knife): 别 began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".
column9: Other people, someone else: 別人的書 "other people's books". Here 別 means "other"; before a verb it means "don't". On the right is 刂 (knife): 別 began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".

column3: Year. Put it after the number: 三年 "three years", 二〇二五年 "the year 2025". It first meant "harvest" and later "year".
column6: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Hànyǔ.
column7: I have studied Chinese for two years.
column9: Year. Put it after the number: 三年 "three years", 二〇二五年 "the year 2025". It first meant "harvest" and later "year".

column3: Month and "moon": 三月 is March, 十二月 December, and 个月 counts months (两个月). It is a picture of a crescent moon. Elsewhere the same shape is not a moon: in 有 it is meat, in 朋 a string of shells.
column9: Month and "moon": 三月 is March, 十二月 December, and 個月 counts months (兩個月). It is a picture of a crescent moon. Elsewhere the same shape is not a moon: in 有 it is meat, in 朋 a string of shells.

column3: Day and "sun". In dates the written form is 日 (三月五日) and speech says 号 (五号). It is a picture of the sun; the stroke in the middle was added to keep it apart from 口.
column4: 十月十三日是我的生日。
column5: 十月十三日是我的生日。
column6: Shíyuè shísān rì shì wǒ de shēngrì.
column9: Day and "sun". In dates the written form is 日 (三月五日) and speech says 號 (五號). It is a picture of the sun; the stroke in the middle was added to keep it apart from 口.

column3: The day of the month in speech: 五号 "the 5th". Also "number", as in a room or ticket number. 口 (mouth) with 丂, a mark for exhaled breath.
column9: The day of the month in speech: 五號 "the 5th". Also "number", as in a room or ticket number. 口 (mouth) with 丂, a mark for exhaled breath.

column3: Day and "sky": 今天, 三天, 天气. The old form was a standing person with the head stressed; the 一 over 大 is what is left of that.
column6: Yī tiān yǒu èrshísì ge xiǎoshí.
column9: Day and "sky": 今天, 三天, 天氣. The old form was a standing person with the head stressed; the 一 over 大 is what is left of that.

column3: Today, literally "this day". The word 今 means "now, this". Time words go before the verb: 今天我不忙.
column9: Today, literally "this day". The word 今 means "now, this". Time words go before the verb: 今天我不忙.

column3: Tomorrow. 明 is 日 (sun) beside 月 (moon): "bright". 明天见！ is a common way of parting.
column9: Tomorrow. 明 is 日 (sun) beside 月 (moon): "bright". 明天見！ is a common way of parting.

column3: Yesterday. In 昨, 日 (sun, day) is the meaning part and 乍 the sound, though zhà no longer sounds like zuó. Like other time words, it goes before the verb.
column7: I didn't go to school yesterday.
column9: Yesterday. In 昨, 日 (sun, day) is the meaning part and 乍 the sound, though zhà no longer sounds like zuó. Like other time words, it goes before the verb.

column3: The day after tomorrow. Here 后 is "after". The row runs 前天, 昨天, 今天, 明天, 后天.
column7: The day after tomorrow is Saturday.
column9: The day after tomorrow. Here 後 is "after". The row runs 前天, 昨天, 今天, 明天, 後天.

column3: The day before yesterday. 前 is "before, front". The 月 in it is not a moon: it is a worn-down 舟 (boat), since 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.
column7: The day before yesterday I was at home.
column9: The day before yesterday. 前 is "before, front". The 月 in it is not a moon: it is a worn-down 舟 (boat), since 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.

column3: This year. Year words go before the verb and need no 在: 今年我学汉语. The set is 去年, 今年, 明年.
column9: This year. Year words go before the verb and need no 在: 今年我學漢語. The set is 去年, 今年, 明年.

column3: Next year: 明 (bright) plus 年, in the same pattern as 明天. Place it before the verb: 明年我去中国.
column7: Next year I want to go to China.
column9: Next year: 明 (bright) plus 年, in the same pattern as 明天. Place it before the verb: 明年我去中國.

column3: Last year. 去 elsewhere means "go", but here it means "gone by": 去年 is not "go year".
column7: Last year I lived in Beijing.
column9: Last year. 去 elsewhere means "go", but here it means "gone by": 去年 is not "go year".

column3: Week. Days are numbered: 星期一 Monday to 星期六 Saturday; Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日, never 星期七. In 星 the top 日 is a worn-down 晶 (a picture of stars); in 期 the 其 gives the sound.
column7: What day of the week is it?
column9: Week. Days are numbered: 星期一 Monday to 星期六 Saturday; Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日, never 星期七. In 星 the top 日 is a worn-down 晶 (a picture of stars); in 期 the 其 gives the sound.

column3: Sunday. The only day not named with a number; the same as 星期天. 日 means "sun, day".
column7: We don't have class on Sunday.
column9: Sunday. The only day not named with a number; the same as 星期天. 日 means "sun, day".

column3: Sunday, the same as 星期日, with 天 ("day") in place of 日. Ask which day with 星期几.
column7: Where do you want to go on Sunday?
column9: Sunday, the same as 星期日, with 天 ("day") in place of 日. Ask which day with 星期幾.

column3: Birthday: 生 ("be born") plus 日 ("day"). 生日快乐 is "happy birthday". 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground.
column9: Birthday: 生 ("be born") plus 日 ("day"). 生日快樂 is "happy birthday". 生 shows a shoot growing out of the ground.

column3: Date on a calendar: 日 (day) plus 期 (a fixed time). Ask 日期是几号？ 期 has 其 as its sound part (qí, close to qī).
column9: Date on a calendar: 日 (day) plus 期 (a fixed time). Ask 日期是幾號？ 期 has 其 as its sound part (qí, close to qī).

column3: Half a year. 半 comes before the measure word, but 年 and 天 need none, so 半年 and 半天; the others do take 个: 半个月, 半个小时.
column7: I studied Chinese for half a year.
column9: Half a year. 半 comes before the measure word, but 年 and 天 need none, so 半年 and 半天; the others do take 個: 半個月, 半個小時.

column3: Half a day, and in speech "a long time": 我等了半天 "I waited ages". 半 needs no 个 here.
column7: I waited for you for ages.
column9: Half a day, and in speech "a long time": 我等了半天 "I waited ages". 半 needs no 個 here.

column3: New Year: 新年好 or 新年快乐 as a greeting. In 新 the 斤 (axe) is on the right: it first meant "chop wood" (the original of 薪 "firewood") and was borrowed for "new".
column9: New Year: 新年好 or 新年快樂 as a greeting. In 新 the 斤 (axe) is on the right: it first meant "chop wood" (the original of 薪 "firewood") and was borrowed for "new".

column3: Early, and "morning": 早 is also the greeting "morning!". 早 before a verb says early: 早睡 "go to bed early". It started as a picture of an acorn. As a way to remember (not history): the sun 日 just above the horizon.
column6: Nǐ jīntiān qǐ de zhēn zǎo.
column7: You got up really early today.
column9: Early, and "morning": 早 is also the greeting "morning!". 早 before a verb says early: 早睡 "go to bed early". It started as a picture of an acorn. As a way to remember (not history): the sun 日 just above the horizon.

column3: Morning. Light 上: zǎoshang. Put the time before the verb and the clock time after: 早上七点. 早上好 is the greeting.
column7: I get up at seven in the morning.
column9: Morning. Light 上: zǎoshang. Put the time before the verb and the clock time after: 早上七點. 早上好 is the greeting.

column3: Morning up to noon: 上午九点. 午 means "noon" (a pestle, unrelated to 干); 上 here means "first half". The pair is 下午.
column7: I have class in the morning.
column9: Morning up to noon: 上午九點. 午 means "noon" (a pestle, unrelated to 干); 上 here means "first half". The pair is 下午.

column3: Noon, midday: 中 (middle) plus 午 (noon). It is the usual time for lunch: 中午吃饭.
column9: Noon, midday: 中 (middle) plus 午 (noon). It is the usual time for lunch: 中午吃飯.

column3: Afternoon: 下 plus 午. The word comes before the clock time: 下午三点, "3 p.m."
column7: I'm going to the shop this afternoon.
column9: Afternoon: 下 plus 午. The word comes before the clock time: 下午三點, "3 p.m."

column3: Late and "evening": 太晚了 "too late". 日 (sun) is the meaning part and 免 the sound (miǎn, close to wǎn). Also in the set phrase 晚上好.
column9: Late and "evening": 太晚了 "too late". 日 (sun) is the meaning part and 免 the sound (miǎn, close to wǎn). Also in the set phrase 晚上好.

column3: Evening, night: 今天晚上 is "tonight". Light 上: wǎnshang. 晚上好 is "good evening".
column7: I watch TV in the evening.
column9: Evening, night: 今天晚上 is "tonight". Light 上: wǎnshang. 晚上好 is "good evening".

column3: Daytime, in contrast to 晚上: 白天上班，晚上休息. Literally "white day", meaning bright day.
column9: Daytime, in contrast to 晚上: 白天上班，晚上休息. Literally "white day", meaning bright day.

column3: Now: 现在几点？ It can come before or after the subject: 现在我很忙 or 我现在很忙. In 现, 王 (jade) is the meaning part and 见 gives the sound, close to xiàn.
column9: Now: 現在幾點？ It can come before or after the subject: 現在我很忙 or 我現在很忙. In 現, 王 (jade) is the meaning part and 見 gives the sound, close to xiàn.

column3: Time, moment: 什么时候 asks "when". After a clause with 的 it means "when": 吃饭的时候. The 候 is light: shíhou.
column9: Time, moment: 什麼時候 asks "when". After a clause with 的 it means "when": 吃飯的時候. The 候 is light: shíhou.

column3: Time as a stretch or amount: 有时间 "have time", 没时间 "have no time". For a clock time say 点: 三点. 间 means "between, space".
column9: Time as a stretch or amount: 有時間 "have time", 沒時間 "have no time". For a clock time say 點: 三點. 間 means "between, space".

column3: Hour as a length of time: 一个小时, 两个小时. A clock hour is 点, not 小时. 时 has 日 (sun) as meaning part. Half an hour is 半个小时, and 钟头 is a spoken synonym.
column6: Wǒ xué le liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
column9: Hour as a length of time: 一個小時, 兩個小時. A clock hour is 點, not 小時. 時 has 日 (sun) as meaning part. Half an hour is 半個小時, and 鐘頭 is a spoken synonym.

column3: A little while, a moment: 等一会儿 "wait a moment". 会儿 is said huìr. 一会儿见 means "see you in a bit". Here 会 is not the verb "can".
column9: A little while, a moment: 等一會兒 "wait a moment". 會兒 is said huìr. 一會兒見 means "see you in a bit". Here 會 is not the verb "can".

column3: Sometimes: 有 ("have") plus 时候 ("times"). It goes before the verb or at the start: 有时候我坐车. The short form is 有时.
column9: Sometimes: 有 ("have") plus 時候 ("times"). It goes before the verb or at the start: 有時候我坐車. The short form is 有時.

column3: Sometimes, the short form of 有时候. It is often paired for contrast: 有时…有时… ("sometimes… sometimes…").
column6: Wǒ yǒushí zuò chē, yǒushí zǒulù.
column7: I sometimes take a bus and sometimes walk.
column9: Sometimes, the short form of 有時候. It is often paired for contrast: 有時…有時… ("sometimes… sometimes…").

column3: Right away, at once: 我马上来. Literally "on horseback": 马 ("horse") plus 上 ("on"). Adding 就 makes it more urgent: 马上就到 "arriving any moment".
column6: Nǐ děng yīxià, wǒ mǎshàng lái.
column7: Wait a moment, I'll be right there.
column9: Right away, at once: 我馬上來. Literally "on horseback": 馬 ("horse") plus 上 ("on"). Adding 就 makes it more urgent: 馬上就到 "arriving any moment".

column3: O'clock: 三点, and 三点半 "half past three". Also "a bit" (一点儿) and "to order" (点菜). 占 gives the sound (zhàn). Before an adjective, 有点儿 means "a little", mostly of something unwelcome: 有点儿贵.
column9: O'clock: 三點, and 三點半 "half past three". Also "a bit" (一點兒) and "to order" (點菜). 占 gives the sound (zhàn). Before an adjective, 有點兒 means "a little", mostly of something unwelcome: 有點兒貴.

column3: Often: 常来 "come often". 巾 (cloth) is the meaning part and 尚 the sound. It first meant a lower garment (now written 裳) and was borrowed for "long-lasting; often".
column7: I often go to that shop.
column9: Often: 常來 "come often". 巾 (cloth) is the meaning part and 尚 the sound. It first meant a lower garment (now written 裳) and was borrowed for "long-lasting; often".

column3: Often, the doubled form of 常: 他常常来. The usual negative is 不常, not 不常常; 常常不 is something else, "often doesn't": 他常常不吃早饭. It goes before the verb.
column6: Tā chángcháng gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
column9: Often, the doubled form of 常: 他常常來. The usual negative is 不常, not 不常常; 常常不 is something else, "often doesn't": 他常常不吃早飯. It goes before the verb.

column3: First, beforehand: 先…再… means "first…, then…": 先吃饭，再看书. 先 is a foot 止 in front of a person 儿 (to go forward).
column9: First, beforehand: 先…再… means "first…, then…": 先吃飯，再看書. 先 is a foot 止 in front of a person 儿 (to go forward).

column3: Again for something that has not happened yet: 再说一次 "say it once more". In 先…再… it means "then". For a repeat that already took place, Chinese uses 又 instead.
column9: Again for something that has not happened yet: 再說一次 "say it once more". In 先…再… it means "then". For a repeat that already took place, Chinese uses 又 instead.

column3: Last time: 上 ("previous") plus 次 ("occasion"). 上 itself is a short stroke above a long one. The next one is 下次.
column7: Where did you go last time?
column9: Last time: 上 ("previous") plus 次 ("occasion"). 上 itself is a short stroke above a long one. The next one is 下次.

column3: Next time: 下次再来 "come again next time". 下 mirrors 上: a short stroke under a long one.
column9: Next time: 下次再來 "come again next time". 下 mirrors 上: a short stroke under a long one.

column3: Eat: 吃饭, 吃面包. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 乞 the sound, though qǐ no longer sounds like chī. 你吃了吗？ is a common greeting.
column9: Eat: 吃飯, 吃麵包. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 乞 the sound, though qǐ no longer sounds like chī. 你吃了嗎？ is a common greeting.

column3: Drink: 喝水, 喝茶. Soup is also 喝, not 吃. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 曷 the sound.
column7: What do you want to drink?
column9: Drink: 喝水, 喝茶. Soup is also 喝, not 吃. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 曷 the sound.

column3: Cooked rice, and so "a meal": 吃饭 is "eat a meal". 饣 (food) is the meaning part and 反 the sound (fǎn, close to fàn).
column9: Cooked rice, and so "a meal": 吃飯 is "eat a meal". 飠 (food) is the meaning part and 反 the sound (fǎn, close to fàn).

column3: Dish eaten with rice, and "vegetable": 点菜 is "order dishes". 艹 (plant) on top is the meaning part and 采 the sound (cǎi, close to cài).
column9: Dish eaten with rice, and "vegetable": 點菜 is "order dishes". 艹 (plant) on top is the meaning part and 采 the sound (cǎi, close to cài).

column3: Tea: 喝茶. 艹 (plant) is the meaning part on top. The modern 茶 comes from an older character for a bitter plant.
column9: Tea: 喝茶. 艹 (plant) is the meaning part on top. The modern 茶 comes from an older character for a bitter plant.

column3: Water: 喝水, 热水. It is a picture of flowing water. At the left of other characters it becomes 氵 (河, 洗, 渴) and 水 also starts 水果.
column9: Water: 喝水, 熱水. It is a picture of flowing water. At the left of other characters it becomes 氵 (河, 洗, 渴) and 水 also starts 水果.

column3: Milk: 牛奶 is cow's milk. 女 (woman) is the meaning part and 乃 gives the sound, nǎi in both. 奶奶 "grandma" (the father's mother) uses it too.
column9: Milk: 牛奶 is cow's milk. 女 (woman) is the meaning part and 乃 gives the sound, nǎi in both. 奶奶 "grandma" (the father's mother) uses it too.

column3: Milk (cow's milk): 牛 plus 奶. 牛 is a picture of a bull's head with two horns and two ears. Drink it with 喝.
column9: Milk (cow's milk): 牛 plus 奶. 牛 is a picture of a bull's head with two horns and two ears. Drink it with 喝.

column3: Cooked rice. 米 is raw rice (grains of rice) and 饭 is "meal". Rice that is still uncooked is just 米.
column9: Cooked rice. 米 is raw rice (grains of rice) and 飯 is "meal". Rice that is still uncooked is just 米.

column3: Bread: 面 ("flour") plus 包 ("wrapped thing"). A slice is 一片面包, and to toast bread is 烤面包.
column7: I eat bread in the morning.
column9: Bread: 麵 ("flour") plus 包 ("wrapped thing"). A slice is 一片麵包, and to toast bread is 烤麵包.

column3: Noodles: 面 ("flour") plus 条 ("strip") plus the spoken ending 儿, giving miàntiáor. 条 is also the measure word for long thin things.
column9: Noodles: 麵 ("flour") plus 條 ("strip") plus the spoken ending 兒, giving miàntiáor. 條 is also the measure word for long thin things.

column3: Steamed bun, usually with a filling: 肉包子. 包 means "wrap", so a 包子 is a wrapped thing; 包 is read as a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹. The 子 is light: bāozi.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chī liǎng ge bāozi.
column7: I'd like to eat two buns.
column9: Steamed bun, usually with a filling: 肉包子. 包 means "wrap", so a 包子 is a wrapped thing; 包 is read as a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹. The 子 is light: bāozi.

column3: Meat: 吃肉, 牛肉. It is a picture of the ribs or a slice of meat. Inside other characters it shrinks to ⺼, as in 脑 (brain).
column9: Meat: 吃肉, 牛肉. It is a picture of the ribs or a slice of meat. Inside other characters it shrinks to ⺼, as in 腦 (brain).

column3: Egg, a chicken's egg: 鸡 ("chicken") plus 蛋 ("egg"). In 蛋, 虫 (insect, creature) is the meaning part. Cooking words come before it: 煮鸡蛋 "boiled egg", 炒鸡蛋 "scrambled egg"; count them with 个.
column6: Wǒ zǎofàn chī yī ge jīdàn.
column7: I eat an egg at breakfast.
column9: Egg, a chicken's egg: 雞 ("chicken") plus 蛋 ("egg"). In 蛋, 虫 (insect, creature) is the meaning part. Cooking words come before it: 煮雞蛋 "boiled egg", 炒雞蛋 "scrambled egg"; count them with 個.

column3: Fruit, as a food: 吃水果. Literally "water fruit". 果 is a picture of fruit growing on a tree (田 above 木). Name the fruit when you mean a particular one.
column9: Fruit, as a food: 吃水果. Literally "water fruit". 果 is a picture of fruit growing on a tree (田 above 木). Name the fruit when you mean a particular one.

column3: Tasty: 好 plus 吃, "good to eat". The same pattern works with other verbs: 好看 "good to look at", 好听 "good to hear", 好玩儿 "fun". The opposite is 难吃.
column9: Tasty: 好 plus 吃, "good to eat". The same pattern works with other verbs: 好看 "good to look at", 好聽 "good to hear", 好玩兒 "fun". The opposite is 難吃.

column3: Eat a meal: a verb plus its object, so it can be split: 吃了饭 "have eaten". 你吃饭了吗？ asks whether someone has eaten.
column9: Eat a meal: a verb plus its object, so it can be split: 吃了飯 "have eaten". 你吃飯了嗎？ asks whether someone has eaten.

column3: Breakfast: 早 ("morning") plus 饭 ("meal"). The three meals are 早饭, 午饭, 晚饭.
column9: Breakfast: 早 ("morning") plus 飯 ("meal"). The three meals are 早飯, 午飯, 晚飯.

column3: Lunch: 午 ("noon") plus 饭. 午 is a picture of a pestle, and has nothing to do with 干.
column9: Lunch: 午 ("noon") plus 飯. 午 is a picture of a pestle, and has nothing to do with 干.

column3: Dinner, supper: 晚 ("evening") plus 饭. The verb is 吃: 吃晚饭.
column9: Dinner, supper: 晚 ("evening") plus 飯. The verb is 吃: 吃晚飯.

column3: Cup, glass. 杯 is the cup and 子 a light noun ending. 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part of 杯 and 不 the sound, though bù only loosely matches bēi.
column7: There is water in the cup.
column9: Cup, glass. 杯 is the cup and 子 a light noun ending. 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part of 杯 and 不 the sound, though bù only loosely matches bēi.

column3: Links a describing word or an owner to a noun: 我的书 "my book", 新的书 "a new book". It sounds like 得 and 地, which do other jobs: 地 comes before a verb (慢慢地走), 得 after a verb (走得快). Light tone: de.
column9: Links a describing word or an owner to a noun: 我的書 "my book", 新的書 "a new book". It sounds like 得 and 地, which do other jobs: 地 comes before a verb (慢慢地走), 得 after a verb (走得快). Light tone: de.

column3: A light particle for something done or new. After a verb: 我吃了饭. At the end of a sentence: 下雨了 "it has started to rain". It marks completion or change, not simply the past. The shape is a picture of a baby without arms.
column6: Wǒ chī le liǎng ge bāozi.
column9: A light particle for something done or new. After a verb: 我吃了飯. At the end of a sentence: 下雨了 "it has started to rain". It marks completion or change, not simply the past. The shape is a picture of a baby without arms.

column3: A particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question: 你是学生吗？ Do not combine it with a question word like 什么 or 谁. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 马 (mǎ) the sound, nearly the same as ma.
column7: Do you have an older brother?
column9: A particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question: 你是學生嗎？ Do not combine it with a question word like 什麼 or 誰. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 馬 (mǎ) the sound, nearly the same as ma.

column3: A light particle for "and what about…?": 我很好，你呢？ Also asks where something is: 我的书呢？ After 在 or 正在 it adds a sense of "right now": 他在吃饭呢. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part.
column9: A light particle for "and what about…?": 我很好，你呢？ Also asks where something is: 我的書呢？ After 在 or 正在 it adds a sense of "right now": 他在吃飯呢. 口 (mouth) is the meaning part.

column3: A light particle that softens a suggestion or a request: 我们走吧 "let's go". Also asks for confirmation: 他是老师吧？ 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 巴 the sound, the same 巴 as in 爸.
column9: A light particle that softens a suggestion or a request: 我們走吧 "let's go". Also asks for confirmation: 他是老師吧？ 口 (mouth) is the meaning part and 巴 the sound, the same 巴 as in 爸.

column3: A light particle after a verb that says a state continues: 门开着 "the door is open", 他坐着 "he is sitting". Taiwan writes it 著; 着, the mainland's form, is not used there.
column9: A light particle after a verb that says a state continues: 門開著 "the door is open", 他坐著 "he is sitting". Taiwan writes it 著; 著, the mainland's form, is not used there.

column3: 1. A particle after a verb, saying you have done it before: 我去过北京 "I have been to Beijing"; the negative is 没去过. 2. A verb, "pass, spend": 过年, 经过, 度过. 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.
column9: 1. A particle after a verb, saying you have done it before: 我去過北京 "I have been to Beijing"; the negative is 沒去過. 2. A verb, "pass, spend": 過年, 經過, 度過. 辶 (walk) is the meaning part.

column3: A light particle that turns a describing word into an adverb before a verb: 慢慢地走 "walk slowly". Read dì it means "ground". Same sound as 的 and 得, so check the position: 地 comes just before the verb.
column9: A light particle that turns a describing word into an adverb before a verb: 慢慢地走 "walk slowly". Read dì it means "ground". Same sound as 的 and 得, so check the position: 地 comes just before the verb.

column3: Right away, as early as, just: 我马上就来; 他八点就来了 "he came already at eight", earlier than expected. 才 is the opposite: 他八点才来 "he didn't come until eight". 就 usually comes with 了, and 才 does not. It goes before the verb.
column6: Tā bā diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
column7: He was already up at eight.
column9: Right away, as early as, just: 我馬上就來; 他八點就來了 "he came already at eight", earlier than expected. 才 is the opposite: 他八點才來 "he didn't come until eight". 就 usually comes with 了, and 才 does not. It goes before the verb.

column3: Still and "also": 他还在家 "he is still at home"; 还有 "there is also". 还 is also read huán "give back". 辶 (walk) is the part on the left in 还.
column9: Still and "also": 他還在家 "he is still at home"; 還有 "there is also". 還 is also read huán "give back". 辶 (walk) is the part on the left in 還.

column3: Just (now), in the middle of doing something: 他正看书呢. Also "upright, correct": 正好 "just right". 止 (foot) is the lower part.
column9: Just (now), in the middle of doing something: 他正看書呢. Also "upright, correct": 正好 "just right". 止 (foot) is the lower part.

column3: In the middle of doing: 我正在吃饭 "I am eating". It goes before the verb and stresses "right now"; 在 alone can mark this too, and 呢 at the end gives a spoken feel.
column9: In the middle of doing: 我正在吃飯 "I am eating". It goes before the verb and stresses "right now"; 在 alone can mark this too, and 呢 at the end gives a spoken feel.

column3: Don't before a verb: 别说话 "don't talk". Also "other" in 别人 and 别的. 刂 (knife) is on the right: it began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".
column9: Don't before a verb: 別說話 "don't talk". Also "other" in 別人 and 別的. 刂 (knife) is on the right: it began as cutting bone from flesh, "to separate".

column3: Some (of them): 有的人 "some people". Often paired: 有的…，有的… "some…, others…". The 的 is light: yǒude.
column9: Some (of them): 有的人 "some people". Often paired: 有的…，有的… "some…, others…". The 的 is light: yǒude.

column3: Come, toward the speaker: 他来了. Before a verb it means "let me do it": 我来介绍一下.
column9: Come, toward the speaker: 他來了. Before a verb it means "let me do it": 我來介紹一下. 來 began as a picture of a wheat plant and was borrowed for "come".

column3: Go, away from the speaker. A place follows directly, with no 到: 去学校, 去北京. There are several ideas for the shape and none is settled.
column9: Go, away from the speaker. A place follows directly, with no 到: 去學校, 去北京. There are several ideas for the shape and none is settled.

column3: Return, go back: 回家, 回学校. It is a spiral, "turning around". With a direction it gives 回来 and 回去.
column7: What time do you go home?
column9: Return, go back: 回家, 回學校. It is a spiral, "turning around". With a direction it gives 回來 and 回去.

column3: Arrive, reach: 到北京, 到家. After a verb it says the goal was reached: 看到, 找到. 至 ("arrive") is the meaning part and 刂 a form of 刀 giving the sound.
column9: Arrive, reach: 到北京, 到家. After a verb it says the goal was reached: 看到, 找到. 至 ("arrive") is the meaning part and 刂 a form of 刀 giving the sound.

column3: Enter: 进门; 进来 "come in", 进去 "go in". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part. The opposite is 出: 出门, 出去 "go out".
column9: Enter: 進門; 進來 "come in", 進去 "go in". 辶 (walk) is the meaning part. The opposite is 出: 出門, 出去 "go out".

column3: Go out, come out: 出门, 出来, 出去. It is a foot 止 stepping out of a pit 凵; the modern shape no longer shows the foot.
column9: Go out, come out: 出門, 出來, 出去. It is a foot 止 stepping out of a pit 凵; the modern shape no longer shows the foot.

column3: Walk, "go", "leave": 我走了 "I'm off". It does not mean "run"; that is 跑. It is a running person (the top was once a different shape), with 止 (foot) added below.
column9: Walk, "go", "leave": 我走了 "I'm off". It does not mean "run"; that is 跑. It is a running person (the top was once a different shape), with 止 (foot) added below.

column3: Run: 跑得很快 "run fast". 走 is "walk" and 跑 only "run". 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 包 the sound (bāo against pǎo).
column7: The child is running on the road.
column9: Run: 跑得很快 "run fast". 走 is "walk" and 跑 only "run". 足 (foot) is the meaning part and 包 the sound (bāo against pǎo).

column3: Sit, and "travel by": 坐车, 坐飞机 "take a bus, a plane". 土 (earth, ground) is its lower part.
column7: I go to Beijing by train.
column9: Sit, and "travel by": 坐車, 坐飛機 "take a bus, a plane". 土 (earth, ground) is its lower part.

column3: Stand, and "station, stop": 车站. 立 ("stand") is the meaning part and 占 the sound (zhàn), the same 占 as in 点 and 店.
column7: He is standing at the door.
column9: Stand, and "station, stop": 車站. 立 ("stand") is the meaning part and 占 the sound (zhàn), the same 占 as in 點 and 店.

column3: Arrive at, come to: 来到北京 "come to Beijing". A place follows directly. It is 来 plus 到, "come and arrive".
column9: Arrive at, come to: 來到北京 "come to Beijing". A place follows directly. It is 來 plus 到, "come and arrive".

column3: Come back, toward the speaker: 他回来了 "he's back". The 来 is light and marks direction: huílai. The opposite is 回去.
column9: Come back, toward the speaker: 他回來了 "he's back". The 來 is light and marks direction: huílai. The opposite is 回去.

column3: Go back, away from the speaker: 我要回去了 "I have to go back". The 去 is light: huíqu. The opposite is 回来.
column6: Tài wǎn le, wǒ yào huíqu le.
column7: It's late, I have to go back.
column9: Go back, away from the speaker: 我要回去了 "I have to go back". The 去 is light: huíqu. The opposite is 回來.

column3: Go home: 回 plus 家, a verb and object, so no 到 or 去 is needed: 我回家. 家 means "home, family".
column9: Go home: 回 plus 家, a verb and object, so no 到 or 去 is needed: 我回家. 家 means "home, family".

column3: Return to: 回到家 "get back home". 到 says the place was reached; a place follows.
column9: Return to: 回到家 "get back home". 到 says the place was reached; a place follows.

column3: Come in, toward the speaker: 请进来. The 来 marks direction.
column7: Please come in and sit down.
column9: Come in, toward the speaker: 請進來. The 來 marks direction.

column3: Go in, away from the speaker: 我们进去吧. The 去 marks direction.
column9: Go in, away from the speaker: 我們進去吧. The 去 marks direction.

column3: Come out: 他出来了. After a verb it can mean "work out, make out": 看出来 "see that".
column7: He came out of the house.
column9: Come out: 他出來了. After a verb it can mean "work out, make out": 看出來 "see that".

column3: Go out: 我出去一下 "I'll step out". The 去 marks a direction away from the speaker.
column7: I'm going out to buy things.
column9: Go out: 我出去一下 "I'll step out". The 去 marks a direction away from the speaker.

column3: Sit down. 下 after a verb often marks downward movement: 坐下. The 下 is light: zuòxia.
column9: Sit down. 下 after a verb often marks downward movement: 坐下. The 下 is light: zuòxia.

column3: Walk, on foot: a verb and its object, 走 ("walk") plus 路 ("road"). 走路去学校 is "walk to school".
column9: Walk, on foot: a verb and its object, 走 ("walk") plus 路 ("road"). 走路去學校 is "walk to school".

column3: Rise, get up: 起床, 起来; and in 一起 "together". 走 (walk) is the meaning part. The right part is one of the look-alikes 己 or 巳, so learn it by copying.
column9: Rise, get up: 起床, 起來; and in 一起 "together". 走 (walk) is the meaning part. The right part is one of the look-alikes 己 or 巳, so learn it by copying.

column3: Get up, stand up: 请起来. After a verb or adjective it means "begin to": 笑起来 "start laughing". The 来 is light: qǐlai.
column9: Get up, stand up: 請起來. After a verb or adjective it means "begin to": 笑起來 "start laughing". The 來 is light: qǐlai.

column3: The general measure word: 一个人, 三个朋友, 两个杯子. When you do not know a noun's measure word, 个 is the safe choice. 个 is half of 竹 (bamboo).
column9: The general measure word: 一個人, 三個朋友, 兩個杯子. When you do not know a noun's measure word, 個 is the safe choice. 個 has 亻 (person) as its meaning part.

column3: The measure word for books and notebooks: 一本书, 两本课本. It is 木 (tree) with an extra stroke at the bottom marking the roots, so "root". The stroke is what tells 本 from 木.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū.
column9: The measure word for books and notebooks: 一本書, 兩本課本. It is 木 (tree) with an extra stroke at the bottom marking the roots, so "root". The stroke is what tells 本 from 木.

column3: Cup and "cupful": 一杯茶 "a cup of tea". 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part and 不 the sound part. 杯子 is the cup itself.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi shuǐ.
column7: Please give me a glass of water.
column9: Cup and "cupful": 一杯茶 "a cup of tea". 木 (tree, wood) is the meaning part and 不 the sound part. 杯子 is the cup itself.

column3: The measure word for times something happens: 一次, 两次, 第一次. It is a person breathing out. Its right part 欠 is also in 歌 and 欢.
column6: Wǒ qù guo liǎng cì Běijīng.
column7: I have been to Beijing twice.
column9: The measure word for times something happens: 一次, 兩次, 第一次. It is a person breathing out. Its right part 欠 is also in 歌 and 歡.

column3: Bag, "wrap", "pack": 书包 "schoolbag", 钱包 "wallet", 包子 "bun". It is a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹.
column6: Wǒ de bāo zài zhuōzi shang.
column7: My bag is on the table.
column9: Bag, "wrap", "pack": 書包 "schoolbag", 錢包 "wallet", 包子 "bun". It is a baby 巳 inside a wrapping 勹.

column3: The measure word for pieces ("一块肉") and, in speech, for money: 三块钱 "three yuan". 土 (earth) is the meaning part and 夬 the sound.
column9: The measure word for pieces ("一塊肉") and, in speech, for money: 三塊錢 "three yuan". 土 (earth) is the meaning part and 鬼 the sound.

column3: Yuan, the written unit of money: 十元. In speech people usually say 块: 十块. It is a person with two lines stressing the head.
column9: Yuan, the written unit of money: 十元. In speech people usually say 塊: 十塊. It is a person with two lines stressing the head.

column3: In speech, a tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is 0.5 yuan. The order of units is 块, 毛, 分. Also "hair, fur"; It is a picture of a feather or hair.
column9: In speech, a tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is 0.5 yuan. The order of units is 塊, 毛, 分. Also "hair, fur"; It is a picture of a feather or hair.

column3: Minute: 三点十分 "ten past three". Also the smallest coin and a point in a score: 九十分. It is 八 ("to divide") over 刀 (knife), separating with a knife.
column9: Minute: 三點十分 "ten past three". Also the smallest coin and a point in a score: 九十分. It is 八 ("to divide") over 刀 (knife), separating with a knife.

column3: Money: 多少钱？ "how much?", 有钱 "rich". 钅 is the metal part, which also stands for money, and 戋 gives the sound.
column7: He has a lot of money.
column9: Money: 多少錢？ "how much?", 有錢 "rich". 釒 is the metal part, which also stands for money, and 戔 gives the sound.

column3: Wallet, purse: 钱 ("money") plus 包 ("bag").
column9: Wallet, purse: 錢 ("money") plus 包 ("bag").

column3: Years of age, after the number: 二十岁. 你几岁？ is how you ask a child. the mountain-like top of 岁 is unrelated to 山.
column7: My son is three years old.
column9: Years of age, after the number: 二十歲. 你幾歲？ is how you ask a child.

column3: Some, a few: 一些人, 一些书, with no measure word. 些 is the plural measure also seen in 这些 and 那些. For a small amount of something uncountable, 一点儿 is used.
column7: There are some books on the table.
column9: Some, a few: 一些人, 一些書, with no measure word. 些 is the plural measure also seen in 這些 and 那些. For a small amount of something uncountable, 一點兒 is used.

column3: A little, a bit: 一点儿水 "a little water". After an adjective it asks for "a bit more": 快一点儿 "a bit faster". The spoken ending 儿 makes it yīdiǎnr. Without 儿, 一点 can also mean "one o'clock".
column7: Please speak a little more slowly.
column9: A little, a bit: 一點兒水 "a little water". After an adjective it asks for "a bit more": 快一點兒 "a bit faster". The spoken ending 兒 makes it yīdiǎnr. Without 兒, 一點 can also mean "one o'clock".

column3: Put after a verb to make it short and casual: 看一下儿 "take a look", 等一下儿 "wait a moment". 下 here counts one try or one action. The ending 儿 is spoken: yīxiàr. Also written 一下.
column9: Put after a verb to make it short and casual: 看一下兒 "take a look", 等一下兒 "wait a moment". 下 here counts one try or one action. The ending 兒 is spoken: yīxiàr. Also written 一下.

column3: Some: 有些人 "some people". Before an adjective it means "somewhat": 有些累 "a bit tired". Compare 有的, used when others are set against the ones named.
column9: Some: 有些人 "some people". Before an adjective it means "somewhat": 有些累 "a bit tired". Compare 有的, used when others are set against the ones named.

column3: There are some: 有一些人. It is 有 plus 一些, and 一些 takes no measure word before its noun. The same 些 appears in 这些 and 那些.
column9: There are some: 有一些人. It is 有 plus 一些, and 一些 takes no measure word before its noun. The same 些 appears in 這些 and 那些.

column3: Few, little: 人很少 "few people". As a verb it means "do less": 少吃 "eat less". It is four dots meaning "a few", borrowing the sound of 小 (three dots).
column9: Few, little: 人很少 "few people". As a verb it means "do less": 少吃 "eat less". It is four dots meaning "a few", borrowing the sound of 小 (three dots).

column3: Many, much: 很多人. A bare 多 before a noun sounds off, so say 很多 or 好多. Before an adjective it asks "how": 多大 "how big, how old", 多远 "how far". It is two pieces of meat, with the 夕 shapes worn down from 肉.
column9: Many, much: 很多人. A bare 多 before a noun sounds off, so say 很多 or 好多. Before an adjective it asks "how": 多大 "how big, how old", 多遠 "how far". It is two pieces of meat, with the 夕 shapes worn down from 肉.

column3: Together, the same as 一起: 我们一块儿去 "let's go together". 块 is also "piece" and "yuan", but here the word is said yīkuàir.
column9: Together, the same as 一起: 我們一塊兒去 "let's go together". 塊 is also "piece" and "yuan", but here the word is said yīkuàir.

column3: Half of something: 吃了一半 "ate half". It is a noun, so it takes no measure word. For a length of time, 半 comes in front: 半年.
column9: Half of something: 吃了一半 "ate half". It is a noun, so it takes no measure word. For a length of time, 半 comes in front: 半年.

column3: Home, family: 我家有四口人. Also the measure word for shops and companies: 一家商店, 一家饭店. 宀 (roof) is the top; what is now written 豕 (pig) below was once a sound part.
column9: Home, family: 我家有四口人. Also the measure word for shops and companies: 一家商店, 一家飯店. 宀 (roof) is the top; what is now written 豕 (pig) below was once a sound part.

column3: At home: 在 plus 家. 他在家 means "he is home". Going home is a different word: 回家. 在家里 means the same.
column9: At home: 在 plus 家. 他在家 means "he is home". Going home is a different word: 回家. 在家裡 means the same.

column3: At home, in the house or family: 家里有四口人. You can also say 在家 "be at home" and 回家 "go home" without 里.
column7: There are a lot of books at home.
column9: At home, in the house or family: 家裡有四口人. You can also say 在家 "be at home" and 回家 "go home" without 裡.

column3: House, flat: 买房子 "buy a house". 房 has 户 (door) as meaning part and 方 as sound part (fāng, close to fáng). The 子 is light: fángzi. For a room inside, the word is 房间.
column9: House, flat: 買房子 "buy a house". 房 has 戶 (door) as meaning part and 方 as sound part (fāng, close to fáng). The 子 is light: fángzi. For a room inside, the word is 房間.

column3: Room: 我的房间. Not the whole house, which is 房子. 间 means "space between". A house has several: 三个房间.
column6: Wǒ de fángjiān zài èr lóu.
column7: My room is on the second floor.
column9: Room: 我的房間. Not the whole house, which is 房子. 間 means "space between". A house has several: 三個房間.

column3: Restroom, toilet, literally "wash-hand room": 洗 plus 手 plus 间. Ask for it with 请问，洗手间在哪儿？
column9: Restroom, toilet, literally "wash-hand room": 洗 plus 手 plus 間. Ask for it with 請問，洗手間在哪兒？

column3: A measure word for rooms: 一间房; also "space between": 房间, 时间, 中间. The 间 is a gate 门 with 日 inside. It also ends 洗手间 "restroom" and 空间 "space".
column6: Zhè ge fángzi yǒu sān jiān fáng.
column9: A measure word for rooms: 一間房; also "space between": 房間, 時間, 中間. The 間 is a gate 門 with 日 inside. It also ends 洗手間 "restroom" and 空間 "space". 間 began as a variant of 閒, which had the moon 月 where 間 has the sun 日.

column3: Door, gate: 开门, 关门. It is a picture of a gate. It frames the middle of many characters: 问, 们, 间, 开.
column9: Door, gate: 開門, 關門. It is a picture of a gate. It frames the middle of many characters: 問, 們, 間, 開.

column3: Doorway, entrance: at the door or just outside it. 口 ("mouth") also means "opening", as in 路口 "crossing".
column6: Xuéxiào ménkǒu yǒu yī ge shāngdiàn.
column7: There is a shop at the school entrance.
column9: Doorway, entrance: at the door or just outside it. 口 ("mouth") also means "opening", as in 路口 "crossing".

column3: Bed: 一张床; 在床上 "in bed". 广 (a house roof shape) plus 木 (wood): it is read as a wooden piece of furniture in a house.
column9: Bed: 一張床; 在床上 "in bed". 广 (a house roof shape) plus 木 (wood): it is read as a wooden piece of furniture in a house.

column3: Get up, out of bed: 起 ("rise") plus 床 ("bed"). A verb and its object, so 起了床 splits it.
column9: Get up, out of bed: 起 ("rise") plus 床 ("bed"). A verb and its object, so 起了床 splits it.

column3: Table, desk: 一张桌子; 桌子上 "on the table". 木 (wood) is the meaning part of 桌. The 子 is light: zhuōzi.
column7: The book is on the table.
column9: Table, desk: 一張桌子; 桌子上 "on the table". 木 (wood) is the meaning part of 桌. The 子 is light: zhuōzi.

column3: Building of several floors, and "floor": 二楼 is the second floor. 木 (wood) is the meaning part and 娄 gives the sound; both are lóu.
column7: My home is on the third floor.
column9: Building of several floors, and "floor": 二樓 is the second floor. 木 (wood) is the meaning part and 婁 gives the sound; both are lóu.

column3: Upstairs: the floor above. 楼上有人 "someone is upstairs". The pair is 楼下.
column9: Upstairs: the floor above. 樓上有人 "someone is upstairs". The pair is 樓下.

column3: Downstairs: the floor below, or the ground outside the building: 在楼下等你.
